key_insight: Scalable DMD identifies dominant 3D flow structures and their temporal dynamics around a Formula 1 front wing while compressing approximately 6 TB of snapshots to 200 GB of modal data.
engineering_relevance: Linking coherent structures to characteristic frequencies can support aerodynamic diagnosis and reduced-order modeling of complex motorsport flows.
method: Simulate the Imperial Front Wing at Re = 2.2 × 10^5 using spectral/hp-element LES in Nektar++.
Apply scalable POD and DMD through the open-source pyLOM framework.
Associate DMD modes with flow mechanisms using point-probe spectra.
evidence_signal: The simulation used 49.72 million degrees of freedom at polynomial order p = 4, with mean lift and drag coefficients differing from reference data by 2.24% and 2.87%; spectral comparisons associated chord-based Strouhal numbers 5.1, 7.5 and 9.3 with distinct flow mechanisms.
watch_item: Validation is reported for one geometry and Reynolds number; transferability to other operating conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Scalable Modal Analysis of the Imperial Front Wing Flow Field
